summary: A tribally administered lookout on the Flathead Reservation in Sanders County, Montana, first built as a cabin about 1935 and now a 1970s timber tower staffed each summer.

facts.design: Present 20-ft treated timber tower with flat cab (1970s); first structure a 14x14 cabin, about 1935

access.note: On the Flathead Indian Reservation and administered by the Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribe. No source describes a public visiting arrangement, so ask the tribe first.

events.note: First structure: a 14x14 cabin, about 1935, per firelookout.com and the tribes' page
The present 20-ft treated timber tower with flat cab replaced the cabin in the 1970s; the register's build field gives 1970
1979 newspaper item about a lookout at Ferry Basin with six years' experience; name not reproduced
Threatened by the McDonald Fire during the 1994 fire season

corrections.why: Register and firelookout.com both describe the present structure as a 20-ft treated timber tower; 4.3 m is about 14 ft. Confirm whether 4.3 m was meant to be the cab height.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register's 1970 build date fits the present tower, which replaced a first 14x14 cabin built about 1935.
The register's 5,641 ft (1,719 m) is about 9 ft below the 5650 ft given by firelookout.com and the tribal page. The record's 1719.4 m follows the register.

sources.title: Fire Lookouts
sources.publisher: Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes, Division of Fish, Wildlife, Recreation and Conservation

notes_for_editor: Built year: the register's 1970 and the sources' 1935 cabin are both correct for different structures, so the story gives both. Staffing: 'staffed every summer' appears on the register and the tribal page, but neither page is dated, so the 2022 as_of was removed (it was the register's registration year). Height: the record's 4.3 m conflicts with the 20-ft tower the sources describe (proposed correction, not applied). Access: administered by the tribes on the reservation; no public visiting arrangement was found, and the story says to check with the tribe first. Elevation difference is under 10 ft. Nominator and lookout staff names are deliberately omitted. The 1979 and 1994 items come from a secondary history site quoting a newspaper and a newsletter; the originals were not checked.
